test_title: PYST 10: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I - GA (Held On: 12 Aug, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: What is the purpose of the 'Melt and Pour' rule introduced in the DMI&SP Policy 2025?

options.text: Importing partially processed steel and finishing it domestically qualifies as “domestic”
Steel exports must include documentation of Indian melting processes
Steel used in government-funded projects is completely manufactured in India
Biometric authentication is required at smelting plants for traceability

solution:
The correct answer is __**Steel used in government-funded projects is completely manufactured in India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **‘Melt and Pour’ rule:** This rule mandates that steel used for **government-funded projects** must be completely manufactured in **India**. It ensures that the steel is melted, poured, and processed entirely within the country.
 
• The rule aims to enhance the usage of domestically produced steel and supports the vision of **Aatmanirbhar Bharat** (self-reliant India), reducing dependency on imported steel. *Hence, the statement is correct.*
 
• This provision is part of the **Domestically Manufactured Iron & Steel Products (DMI&SP) Policy 2025**, which seeks to promote the domestic steel industry and ensure the quality of steel used in critical projects.
 
• The rule prevents practices such as importing partially processed steel and finishing it domestically to classify it as "domestic." Instead, it strictly requires complete domestic production. *Hence, Option 1 is incorrect.*
 
• Documentation of Indian melting processes for exports is not a requirement under the ‘Melt and Pour’ rule, making *Option 2 incorrect.*
 
• Biometric authentication at smelting plants is not a part of this rule, which makes *Option 4 incorrect.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Domestically Manufactured Iron & Steel Products (DMI&SP) Policy:**

 
 
• The **DMI&SP Policy** was introduced by the Ministry of Steel, Government of India, to ensure the use of domestically produced steel in government-funded projects.
 
• This policy contributes to the growth of the **Indian steel industry**, which plays a critical role in infrastructure development, manufacturing, and economic growth.
 
• The policy aligns with the government’s **Make in India** initiative, ensuring that domestic industries benefit from government procurement.
 
 
 
• **Features of the ‘Melt and Pour’ Rule:**
 
 
• It establishes strict guidelines for steel production processes, ensuring that the steel used in government projects is melted and poured in **India**.
 
• This prevents the misuse of classifications and guarantees the authenticity of domestically manufactured steel.
 
• The rule helps maintain **quality standards** and boosts the competitiveness of Indian steel manufacturers.
 
 
 
• **Applications of the DMI&SP Policy:**
 
 
• The policy is applicable to government-funded projects, including infrastructure projects such as highways, bridges, railways, and power plants.
 
• It promotes the use of domestic steel in sectors like **construction**, **defense**, and **energy**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **India’s Steel Industry:**

 
 
• India is the **second-largest steel producer** in the world, with an annual production capacity exceeding **100 million tonnes**.
 
• The industry contributes significantly to the country’s **GDP** and provides employment to millions.
 
 
 
• **Government Initiatives:**
 
 
• The government has launched initiatives like **National Steel Policy 2017** to enhance production capacity and support sustainable practices.
 
• The DMI&SP Policy is a vital part of these efforts, ensuring the growth and competitiveness of the domestic steel industry.
